title: The Interconnectedness Coefficient: A Semi-Local Graph-Theoretic Measure for Connector Vertices between Cohesive Network Regions
summary: The paper introduces the Interconnectedness Coefficient (IC), a bounded semi-local node measure for connector vertices between locally cohesive network regions, defined as the product of low focal clustering and high mean leave-one-out cohesion behind adjacent vertices. It derives range and extremal properties and uses exact graph families to calibrate maxima, cohesion defects, hub-extension robustness, and a fragmentation threshold, then applies the score to a Human Interactome Map. The central exact result relevant to the target is that the connector x in the hub-extended bridge family Hp,q,r has IC(x)=2/3 and is the unique global maximizer over V≥2.

claims.statement: In the hub-extended bridge family Hp,q,r with p,q ≥ 3 and r ≥ 1, the connector vertex x has IC(x)=2/3 and is the unique global IC maximizer over V≥2.
claims.table_ref: Eq. (14); Table 1, row Connector x; Proposition 3
claims.config_for_value: Construct Bp,q from cliques Kp and Kq (p,q ≥ 3) with gateways a,b; add x adjacent to a,b; add hub s adjacent to x and to r ≥ 1 leaves.
claims.est_compute: CPU, <1 s for a small synthetic instance (e.g., p=q=3, r=1)
claims.quote: For all integers p, q ≥3 and r ≥1, x is the unique global maximizer of the IC over V≥2 in Hp,q,r.

claims.statement: In the two-sided bridge graph Bp,q with p,q ≥ 3, the connector x attains the maximum IC(x)=1.
claims.config_for_value: Vertex-disjoint cliques Kp and Kq with gateways a and b; x is adjacent to a and b; p,q ≥ 3.
claims.quote: For p, q ≥3, C(x) = 0 and Ca\x = Cb\x = 1. Therefore IC(x) = 1.

claims.statement: In the density-controlled windmill family Jc,h,r, the unique IC maximizer is x for c=1, while for c≥2 the maximizer set shifts to {a,b}; the fragmentation threshold is at c=2.
claims.metric: IC maximizer identity / fragmentation threshold c
claims.unit: c threshold (branch multiplicity; c=2 is first fragmented case)
claims.config_for_value: Jc,h,r with c ≥ 1 leaf groups per branch, h ≥ 3 vertices per group, r ≥ 1 leaves on hub s; c=1 gives complete branch, c≥2 fragments each branch-side neighborhood into c groups.
claims.quote: For all integers c ≥1, h ≥3, and r ≥1, the unique IC maximizer is x when c = 1, whereas the maximizer set is {a, b} when c ≥2.

match_target.why: Cheapest central target: the analytic Hp,q,r family needs no dataset download or training, and checking IC(x)=2/3 plus uniqueness over V≥2 directly verifies the hub-extension theorem the user named.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: the target is a bounded IC score printed in [0,1], with no std over repeated runs and no test-set sampling; use the 0.02 absolute band for [0,1]-scale bounded scores.

requirements.stmt: Restrict the ranked candidate set to vertices with degree at least two; do not assign ranks to degree-0 or degree-1 vertices.
requirements.quote: Vertices outside V≥2 are not ranked. This is the minimal structural restriction required for a connector to possess at least two incident directions.

requirements.stmt: Compute the ordinary local clustering coefficient C(v) as 2e(N(v))/(d(v)(d(v)-1)) for d(v)≥2 and set C(v)=0 for d(v)<2.
requirements.quote: we set C(v) = 0 because there is no pair of neighbors on which a nontrivial local clustering value can be based.

requirements.stmt: For an ordered adjacent pair (u,v), compute leave-one-out clustering C_u\v on N(u) after removing v, using denominator (d(u)-1)(d(u)-2) for d(u)≥3, and 0 otherwise.
requirements.quote: Removing the focal vertex from this branch-side neighborhood prevents the connection uv from artificially lowering the cohesion assigned to an otherwise cohesive branch.

requirements.stmt: Average leave-one-out clustering over all neighbors of v: CLOO(v)=1/d(v) sum over u in N(v) of C_u\v, not a sum.
requirements.quote: The use of a mean rather than a sum is deliberate.

requirements.stmt: Define IC(v)=(1-C(v)) CLOO(v) for every v in V≥2.
requirements.quote: The focal factor 1 −C(v) rewards low clustering among the immediate neighbors of v.

requirements.stmt: Implement and test the exact maximum equality condition: IC(v)=1 only when C(v)=0 and every adjacent leave-one-out term equals 1.
requirements.quote: IC(v) = 1 if and only if C(v) = 0 and Cu\v = 1 for every u ∈N(v).

requirements.stmt: Use triangle counts and common-neighbor intersections so that e(N(u) without v)=T(u)-t(u,v) with t(u,v)=|N(u)∩N(v)|.
requirements.quote: Removing v from N(u) removes exactly the t(u, v) edges joining v to common neighbors

requirements.stmt: Construct Hp,q,r by adding to Bp,q a hub s with r leaf neighbors and the edge sx; x remains adjacent to gateways a and b.
requirements.quote: Form the hub-extended bridge family Hp,q,r from Bp,q by adding a vertex s with r leaf neighbors and the edge sx

requirements.stmt: For Hp,q,r set C(x)=0, the two clique-gateway leave-one-out terms to 1, the hub-direction term to 0, and average to get IC(x)=2/3.
requirements.quote: The two clique gateways remain maximally cohesive after exclusion of x, while the direction through the hub s has leave-one-out clustering zero.

requirements.stmt: Ensure the hub s has IC=0 and leaves are outside V≥2; increasing r must not change IC(x).
requirements.quote: Increasing r raises the degree of s without creating cohesive structure behind its leaf neighbors.

requirements.stmt: Verify uniqueness by comparing x only against positive competitors: gateways with IC=2(m-1)/m^2 ≤3/8 for m≥4 and 0 for m=3.
requirements.quote: Table 1 leaves only the two clique gateways as potential positive competitors.

requirements.stmt: Return IC values as dimensionless scores on [0,1], not percentages.
requirements.quote: The IC is dimensionless and bounded between zero and one.
